captions.text: Valet on the Mac, and the iPhone app in the Simulator. Both talk through Valet’s relay, running locally here.
To pair, open Settings › Devices on the Mac and choose Pair an iPhone.
The Mac shows a one-time QR code. The Simulator has no camera, so this test build reads the same code over a local link.
The phone shows six digits. The Mac shows three codes, and you pick the one that matches the phone.
Picking it asks for Touch ID on the Mac (this test build answers that itself). The phone is paired.
Now an agent, connected to Valet over MCP, writes an adapter for a made-up library site.
Installing it needs your approval. The request is sealed to the phone and sent through the relay.
The card on the phone says what the adapter can reach and who asked. Approve asks for Face ID.
Approved with Face ID on the phone. The signed approval goes back to the Mac, which checks it and installs.
The agent asks how its request went: approved, and the adapter is installed.
Next the agent asks to keep call traces for 3 days instead of 14. Shortening them removes evidence, so it needs an approval.
This time you decline on the phone, with a note for the agent. No Face ID is needed to say no.
The agent is told it was declined, and gets your note. Nothing changed.
Without a paid Apple developer account there are no push notifications. Here the phone app is closed when the agent asks.
The Mac keeps the request until the phone confirms it has it.
Open Valet on the phone and it reconnects. The waiting card arrives straight away.
Approved with Face ID, same as before.
Every request, approval and decline is in the Mac’s audit log.
